references.text: God threatens to strike Pharaoh's firstborn if he refuses to let Israel go - the same pattern of threat with plague upon refusal
The fulfillment of the threat of the frog plague that comes over all the land of Egypt
Similar wording where God threatens with plague if Pharaoh refuses to let the people go
The same pattern with a threat of locust plague over the entire borders of the land if Pharaoh refuses
The psalmist recalls the frog plague that God sent upon Egypt
Poetic retelling of the frog plague that filled all of Egypt, including the king's chambers
Unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon and the beast and the false prophet - an allusion to Egypt's frog plague
Direct narrative connection: 8:17 is an early warning in the same sequence of plagues as 7:27.
Direct narrative connection: 9:15 escalates the threat from 7:27 from 'plague' to 'total destruction'.
